title: PRESSER | Trinidad Chambliss - MSU Postgame (11-27-26)
text: Trinidad, you know, last home game at Old Miss. What do you think your legacy here at Miss has been? >> Um, just hope that, you know, everyone that I came across and uh encountered with on a day-to-day life here, um, that they can just say, you know, positive things and good things about me and my family and, you know, the last name on my back. Um, I hope I represented my family well. Um, and just, you know, being remembered as a guy who, you know, showed up with a smile on his face. um you know brought positivity to you know the team and uh the people around him and um just you know fought his tail off and you know was just a team player and just loved to compete. >> What were your emotions and thoughts throughout the week and maybe today going into today? Yeah. Um a little emotional, you know, past couple weeks. I mean, just kind of soaking it all in, embracing it, and just, you know, cherishing every moment really cuz um you know, you don't get these times back and you know, life goes on and you know, just trying to create as many memories and as many good positive um experiences as I can and um I definitely did, I would say. >> What are the next few weeks look like for you? Obviously, you said you're going to play in the bowl game, but I'd imagine you also have some draft prep going on. >> Yeah, for sure. I'm definitely going to figure out, you know, [clears throat] what my, you know, plan will be, you know, moving forward, um, you know, after the bowl game and, you know, figuring out where I'll be and, um, who I'll be, you know, working with. Um, but, you know, right now, just going to enjoy, you know, the Egg Bowl, um, you know, this win with my guys and, you know, soak this in as much as I can and then, you know, obviously do bowl prep, um, when when those days come and, you know, hopefully get one more win, you know, in the Old Miss uniform. You know, >> you're not someone who started at Miss, but you've you've won two Egg Bowls. just what what what does it mean to to win this game? >> Means a lot. Um you know me being from Michigan um you know I I kind of knew that you know as a rivalry um but you know meeting the people who are from and you know born and raised in Mississippi you know it means it means more to them. Um you know it's it's a historical game. Um there's a lot of you know you know deep passion for this game too and you know it means a lot for people who come through Mississippi State and Old Miss. So, um, to put on the Old Miss uniform, I wear it with pride and I'm glad that, you know, we got the win and I'm 2 and0 against Mississippi State. So, um, glad about that. >> I see your your mom right there. I hope your dad recovering from surgery and all right. Hope he's doing well, but how cool is it and how meaningful has it been to to have your family a part of so many Oxford memories? >> It's it's super special. Um it's something that you know I work so hard for is um you know they s they sacrificed so much for me and my family and you know they've you know took a lot out of their day and you know their time and energy and poured in so much into me and you know even when it came back to when I was you know 5 years old or you know 8 years old and just sacrificing their time and money you know for training sessions and workouts and stuff and travel all that is you know coming to fruition now with them you know enjoying the fruits of you know being at a miss game and you know their sons being the quarterback of you know a big program and you know going to the college football playoff last year and you know being at these fun games and it's awesome to see the people interact and just embrace them as well and just love them and support them as much as as much as me too. So um I love them so much you know love my mom, love my dad, love my family. Um I'm glad that I'm able to you know I guess provide you know a life where they can enjoy as well you know and that that only comes from them supporting me and just being there by my side. >> Take questions up top. Yeah, Trinidad, the offensive execution maybe in the first half maybe not what you would have wanted, but in the second half you guys kind of dominated, I guess. What do you take from the first half and the second half negatives or positives? [clears throat] >> We were kind of just shooting ourselves in the foot in the first half. Um, you know, the plays were there. Um, we just didn't make the plays. Um, and, you know, it was only a matter of time when when, you know, those plays were going to, you know, go our way and things were going to things were going to click. Um, but yeah, I mean, our offense is super explosive. Um, you know, my guys, you know, make plays whenever, you know, they get open in space and, you know, it's my job to give them the ball. So, um, just happy for them and happy for, you know, their fight. Um, because it could be, you know, it could have been different, honestly. I mean, you know, Mississippi State came with it. Um, but yeah, proud of the way we came in the second half. >> We'll stay up top. >> Yeah. Trinidad, after you got the trophy, you spent time with uh the student section, then you went over the homeside crowd. Uh, why did you feel like it was important to share that moment with everybody in the stadium? I mean, cuz everyone's, you know, a part of this. It's not just me. It's not just my teammates. It's not just our coaches. It's, you know, every fan, every supporter, every booster, everyone. Um, you know, we're all in it together. And that's what it is. So, um, I feel like it was, you know, my job and, you know, my honor to, you know, share that moment with the the fans as well. And, you know, they sacrifice, you know, their time and energy to come out here and to watch us and, you know, pay good money to come see us. So, um, you know, I want to make it, you know, be known and make it be, I guess, an experience of a lifetime, you know, to come see me play and see my teammates play so that they'll always remember. So, um, yeah, that's always, you know, about, you know, everyone, you know, everyone's in this together. So, that was, you know, the main reason. >> Trinidad, uh, obviously your time here is is nearing its end. If you could pinpoint something that you can go to in your mind that you'll miss the most, what would that be? >> Like my greatest memory here? Yeah, >> there's so many. Um, definitely the Sugar Bowl. I would say last year, um, just everything that kind of went into last year too with, you know, people saying that we weren't going to be as good as, you know, previous Old Miss teams and, you know, we were really listening to that. you know, we just, you know, had our head down and, you know, just showed up every day, you know, worked hard and, you know, everyone just like loved to play football. Um, and just supported each other and that was just truly special like all the hard work and dedication that, you know, everyone put in, you know, to the whole year cuz it's more than just, you know, showing up, you know, August 30th on our first game. You know, it's spring ball, summer, um, and then obviously the season, but, you know, just so much time and energy that people don't see, uh, behind closed doors that, you know, goes into a football season. So, um, that was probably my biggest and, uh, most memorable experience is the Sugar Bowl. >> How important has Joe Judge been to you over these last two years? >> Yeah. Um, that's a friend for life and, um, one of the greatest coaches that I'll probably encounter in my life as well, too. Um, he's taught me so much about football, but also in life, too. Um, you know, he's a great figure that I look up to as well. Um, he reminds me a lot of my dad. Uh, so I I think that makes sense. um you know just always you know you know finding ways to you know help me in any situation um regardless if it's football or or it's life. Um and yeah, I'm uh I'm truly uh just truly grateful to you know meet him and just have a relationship with him. Um and yeah, that's a friend for life. So I'm just truly grateful. Sam, >> now that you're you're done playing in Oxford, is uh you will have to move pretty soon, I guess, for the combine and all that. Is is the plan still to to keep your house and and keep Old Miss a part of your life? keep Oxford a part of your life? >> 100%. Yeah. I mean, you know, I've said before, you know, miss and Oxford is home, you know, forever now. Um, the way they embrace me, the way they embrace my family is, um, unlike no other, and I've never experienced anything like that really. Um, so it's truly awesome to see, you know, people that even aren't related to you, you know, feel like family and that's what it is. So, definitely keeping the house. Um, and I'm excited to come back, you know, after my, you know, hopefully long NFL career is over. uh coming back to the you know Grove and experience that as you know I guess a regular you know non-athlete. So um yeah I I can't wait for that. >> Coach talked about your smile and your contagious personality. Where does your joy and positivity come from? [clears throat] >> I would definitely say uh my family, my parents for sure. Um probably more like my mom. She's just always having a positive mindset about everything. I don't know how she does it. Um cuz she's been through a lot. Um, and I actually talked about her or talked about her or talked to her about this is like my like what do you like how do you always like have like a positive mindset like how do you always like see like I guess the brighter side of things and she just was saying like life goes on like she's experienced so much and you know she finds a way to kind of just you know I cope and just you know be grateful for like even the smallest things. So you know I look up to that um and that's something I got to work on too cuz uh you know I'll get down about some things but you know she always you know picks me back up so I definitely get it from her. >> All right we'll wrap it. Thanks guys. Appreciate it. >> All right. Appreciate you guys. Thank you.
